messages.subject: Re: Utility function to set package options
messages.subject_clean: Utility function to set package options
messages.body_plain:
Why not just use options(packagename.optionname) ?

Hadley

On Sat, Feb 28, 2015 at 1:21 PM, Luca Cerone <luca....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi everybody, when writing my functions I always find myself using
> a function "pkgoptions" I wrote, which I find quite handy to set and
> retrieve options package.
>
> When I need some way to set and retrieve options in my package I do the
> following:
>
> mypkgopt <- pkgoptions()
>
> After that in my code I can set options using mypkgopt("option_name",
> option_value).
>
> I retrieve the options I have set using mypkgopt("optionname")
>
> And if I want to see all the values I use mypkgopt()
>
> I have tried to check whether a similar function was already implemented in
> devtools,
> but I couldn't find it.
>
> I think due to its generality and utility this function would fit well in
> devtools (if it is not redundant, if not I would rather learn the "devtools"
> way).
>
> Since I use devtools mostly as a user I don't have a fork of the repository
> so I am attacching the file here,
> but of course if you think it is useful enough to include it and  prefer
> that I submit a branch request I can do that.
>
> If you think it is a bad approach I am willing to learn why :)
>
> Cheers,
> Luca
>

messages.subject: Re: system.file has disappeard.
messages.body_plain:
When you run load_all() on your package, the devtools:::shim_system.file function gets inserted into your package's imports environment, with the name system.file. So if any functions in your package call system.file(), they'll see the shimmed version (when your package is loaded with load_all()).

It's not exported because there's not a reason for most users to call that function directly -- the original intended purpose of the function was only to be used as a shim as described above. The fact that devtools::system.file was exported in the past was because we had not yet thought of the current (cleaner) way of adding shims.

-Winston

messages.subject: Help improving documentation of related functions:
messages.subject_clean: Help improving documentation of related functions:
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

in one of my packages I have two functions fun_a and fun_b defined in a way similar to this:

#' @rdname fun
#'
#' @name fun_a
#'
#' @title function A
#'
#' @description what function A does
#'
#' @param x variable required in input
#'
#' @export
#'
fun_a <- function(x, ...){
    --- code
    return(res)
}

#' @rdname fun
#'
#' @name fun_b
#'
#' @title function b
#'
#' @description what function A does
#'
#' @export
fun_b <- function(...){
    res <- fun_a(...)
    -- manipulate a bit res
    -- return the modified result.
    return(res)
}

When I run document(),
the Usage section appears like

fun_a( x, ...)

fun_b(...)

I would like to override the Usage of fun_b to be
fun_b(x,...).

Is this possible? How can I do this?

Thanks a lot in advance to all of you for the help,

Cheers,
Luca

Sorry, for the spam I finally found out how to do it.

When I opened RStudio, I was exposed to a nice @usage roclet that does the trick.

In the specific example one has to add:

@usage fun_b(x,...)

While this does the trick, I was wondering, is there some more elegant way have exactly the formals defined in fun_a? this way if I change the syntax for fun_a I have to remember to copy and paste it into @usage in fun_b, which I
would prefer to avoid.

Cheers,
Luca

Sorry, for the spam I finally found out how to do it.

When I opened RStudio, I was exposed to a nice @usage roclet that does the trick.

In the specific example one has to add:

@usage fun_b(x,...)
